findings.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:193-199: enableSqlExpressions is a hardcoded stub that always returns false, ignoring the computed 'enabled' variable; combined with the ReadQuery guard, every QueryTypeSQL request unconditionally fails with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented', making the SQL expression query type dead on arrival and the feature flag toggle non-functional

pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12-23: The PR removes the working go-duck DuckDB implementation and replaces it with stubs whose TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto unconditionally return 'not implemented' errors, breaking SQLCommand.Execute (sql_command.go:101) and TablesList (parser.go:23-24) at runtime — a regression from previously functional behavior

pkg/expr/reader.go:131: The error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is misleading when the feature flag is actually enabled, since the stub always returns false — the message masks the actual condition and gives no indication a config flag exists or the check logic is broken

SQL injection pattern in TablesList: user-supplied SQL is string-interpolated into a command passed to RunCommands with only single-quote escaping, which is not a safe escaping strategy for DuckDB string literals; should use parameterized queries or a proper quoting API (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23-25)

Feature flag logic is inverted/broken in reader.go:193-199 — the condition uses ! and the function returns false on both branches, so SQL expression queries can never be enabled and are unconditionally rejected
Cross-package call to unexported function: pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96 calls sql.NewInMemoryDB() which is unexported in package sql, causing a compile break; the export was likely accidentally dropped

Error message misleads users about state: reader.go:129 returns generic 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error instead of a feature-flag-disabled/ErrUnsupported-style error, so orgs that explicitly enable FlagSqlExpressions can't distinguish 'disabled' from 'broken'

enableSqlExpressions in pkg/expr/reader.go:193-198 always returns false because the feature flag check is broken — both branches return false and the enabled assignment is dead, so every QueryTypeSQL expression returns 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' regardless of configuration

QueryFramesInto was replaced with a permanent stub: SQLCommand.Execute (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-100) and the DB in pkg/expr/sql/db.go:17-19 always fail with 'not implemented', and TablesList and RunCommands (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23-26) always error, so every SQL expression execution fails at runtime

Per-request in-memory DB construction with no pooling/reuse: sql.NewInMemoryDB() is constructed on every Execute call (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96), a significant per-request cost for a real engine; should reuse a pooled instance or document the single-shot pattern

Unbounded frame materialization into a single in-memory DB (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-99): allFrames are loaded wholesale into the DB with no row/size limit, doubling memory for large results with no cap or spill path, baking an unbounded API contract into the seam

TablesList relies on a string-escaped SQL round-trip via json_serialize_sql per call (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23-26), doing per-expression per-request query-parse work that could be cached, and creating a correctness surface with escape-based SQL string building

enableSqlExpressions in pkg/expr/reader.go:193-199 computes an inverted enabled value and then ignores it, returning false in both branches, so SQL expressions are unconditionally rejected even when the feature flag is enabled, and unit tests masking this

Stub DB in pkg/expr/sql/db.go:13-23 returns errors.New("not implemented") for TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto, making all SQL-expression execution dead at runtime after removal of the go-duck dependency

Misleading error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" at pkg/expr/reader.go:131 is surfaced to API callers with no wrapped context, misattributing a configuration/feature-maturity issue to a missing implementation

Unreachable broken path in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:20-30: TablesList builds the json_serialize_sql command and calls the stub RunCommands which always errors, leaving dead/rotting escaping logic untestable against a real backend

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/expr/reader.go:131: The error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is misleading when the feature flag is actually enabled, since the stub always returns false — the message masks the actual condition and gives no indication a config flag exists or the check logic is broken

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, ReadQuery now gates QueryTypeSQL on enableSqlExpressions(h). But enableSqlExpressions is implemented to always return false (it computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` and returns false in both branches). This makes SQL expressions always fail with `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` regardless of the feature flag state, and the message is misleading because it suggests missing implementation rather than a disabled/broken flag check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection pattern in TablesList: user-supplied SQL is string-interpolated into a command passed to RunCommands with only single-quote escaping, which is not a safe escaping strategy for DuckDB string literals; should use parameterized queries or a proper quoting API (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23-25)

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go`, `rawSQL` is embedded into a single-quoted SQL string literal (`fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)`) after replacing `'` with `''`. Doubling single quotes is the standard/appropriate escaping mechanism for SQL string literals, so the diff does not clearly show an injectable breakout from the literal into executable SQL. The finding’s claim that this is an unsafe escaping strategy for DuckDB string literals is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feature flag logic is inverted/broken in reader.go:193-199 — the condition uses ! and the function returns false on both branches, so SQL expression queries can never be enabled and are unconditionally rejected

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions() is implemented to always return false: it sets enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions), then if enabled { return false } and then returns false unconditionally. ReadQuery() for QueryTypeSQL calls this and rejects when !enabled, so SQL expression queries are always rejected regardless of the feature flag state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cross-package call to unexported function: pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96 calls sql.NewInMemoryDB() which is unexported in package sql, causing a compile break; the export was likely accidentally dropped

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` in package `sql` with an exported constructor `func NewInMemoryDB() *DB` (capital N). Therefore `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` calling `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` is a valid cross-package call and should not fail to compile due to unexported visibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error message misleads users about state: reader.go:129 returns generic 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error instead of a feature-flag-disabled/ErrUnsupported-style error, so orgs that explicitly enable FlagSqlExpressions can't distinguish 'disabled' from 'broken'

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, SQL queries are gated by enableSqlExpressions(h), and when it returns false the code returns fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented"). That message does not indicate the feature flag is disabled. Moreover, enableSqlExpressions as added always returns false (it sets enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...) and returns false in all branches), so even if FlagSqlExpressions is enabled globally, callers still get the same generic "not implemented" error and cannot distinguish disabled vs broken/unsupported behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: QueryFramesInto was replaced with a permanent stub: SQLCommand.Execute (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-100) and the DB in pkg/expr/sql/db.go:17-19 always fail with 'not implemented', and TablesList and RunCommands (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23-26) always error, so every SQL expression execution fails at runtime

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the prior DuckDB implementation with a new in-package `sql.DB` stub: `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` methods `TablesList`, `RunCommands`, and `QueryFramesInto` all unconditionally return `errors.New("not implemented")`. `SQLCommand.Execute` now calls `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` and then `db.QueryFramesInto(...)`, which will always error. Likewise `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` now uses `NewInMemoryDB()` and then `RunCommands`, which will always error. Additionally, `enableSqlExpressions` in `pkg/expr/reader.go` always returns `false`, causing `ReadQuery` to reject `QueryTypeSQL` with "sqlExpressions is not implemented". Net effect: SQL expressions cannot be parsed or executed successfully.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-request in-memory DB construction with no pooling/reuse: sql.NewInMemoryDB() is constructed on every Execute call (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96), a significant per-request cost for a real engine; should reuse a pooled instance or document the single-shot pattern

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `SQLCommand.Execute` constructs a new in-memory DB instance on every call (`db := sql.NewInMemoryDB()` in `pkg/expr/sql_command.go`). There is no reuse/pooling mechanism shown, so the per-request construction pattern is real. While the claim about “significant cost” can’t be verified from this diff (the current `NewInMemoryDB` returns an empty stub), the architectural concern about repeated instantiation is diff-grounded and specific.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded frame materialization into a single in-memory DB (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-99): allFrames are loaded wholesale into the DB with no row/size limit, doubling memory for large results with no cap or spill path, baking an unbounded API contract into the seam

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows `SQLCommand.Execute` passing `allFrames` into `db.QueryFramesInto(...)` (pkg/expr/sql_command.go), but it does not show any frame materialization or in-memory loading behavior. In fact, the newly added `pkg/expr/sql/db.go` implements `QueryFramesInto` as `return errors.New("not implemented")`, so no loading/doubling of memory can be verified from this PR. The claim about an unbounded contract and memory growth is therefore not demonstrable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TablesList relies on a string-escaped SQL round-trip via json_serialize_sql per call (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23-26), doing per-expression per-request query-parse work that could be cached, and creating a correctness surface with escape-based SQL string building

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList builds a SQL command via fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL) after manually escaping quotes with strings.Replace(rawSQL, "'", "''", -1). This is verifiable from the diff and does introduce a broader correctness/perf surface (string-building + per-call parsing work) that could be improved (e.g., safer parameterization or caching), but it’s not a directly provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: enableSqlExpressions in pkg/expr/reader.go:193-199 computes an inverted enabled value and then ignores it, returning false in both branches, so SQL expressions are unconditionally rejected even when the feature flag is enabled, and unit tests masking this

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, the newly added enableSqlExpressions() always returns false: it sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false in both the `if enabled` branch and the final return. As a result, in ReadQuery() under QueryTypeSQL, `enabled := enableSqlExpressions(h)` will always be false and the code will always return `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")`, unconditionally rejecting SQL expressions regardless of the feature flag state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stub DB in pkg/expr/sql/db.go:13-23 returns errors.New("not implemented") for TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto, making all SQL-expression execution dead at runtime after removal of the go-duck dependency

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the go-duck dependency and replaces it with a new pkg/expr/sql/db.go where DB.TablesList, DB.RunCommands, and DB.QueryFramesInto all return errors.New("not implemented"). Those methods are invoked by sql/parser.go (TablesList calls NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands) and by pkg/expr/sql_command.go (Execute calls sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto), so SQL-expression parsing/execution would fail at runtime if reached. Additionally, ExpressionQueryReader now blocks QueryTypeSQL with an error via enableSqlExpressions(h), which currently always returns false, further confirming SQL expressions are effectively non-functional in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Misleading error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" at pkg/expr/reader.go:131 is surfaced to API callers with no wrapped context, misattributing a configuration/feature-maturity issue to a missing implementation

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, the new QueryTypeSQL gate returns `eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` when `enableSqlExpressions(h)` is false, which is a feature-flag/configuration condition rather than necessarily an implementation gap. The error is returned directly (no wrapping/context), so callers will see this potentially misleading message without indicating that a feature flag is disabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unreachable broken path in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:20-30: TablesList builds the json_serialize_sql command and calls the stub RunCommands which always errors, leaving dead/rotting escaping logic untestable against a real backend

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList now calls NewInMemoryDB() from the same package (added in pkg/expr/sql/db.go). That DB's RunCommands method is a stub that always returns `errors.New("not implemented")`, so TablesList will deterministically fail if invoked. This makes the command-building/escaping logic effectively dead and breaks previously working behavior that used `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck`. (Even though SQL expressions are currently gated off by enableSqlExpressions always returning false, the implementation as written is still broken when reached.)
